clue.text: Very important circular shortly to be distributed

indicators.note: letters to be distributed are dealt out in a new order, so the shortened word is rearranged
shortly says the word circular is cut short, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: An office memo of great importance is about to be handed round to all staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims circular to CIRCULA, and 'to be distributed' rearranges those seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crucial means decisive or vital, a straightforward synonym for very important.

clue.text: Projection supported by pollster at first is exaggerated

indicators.note: in a down clue, supported by means the first piece sits on top of the next one

parts.note: a cam is a projection on a rotating wheel or shaft in machinery

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word pollster

explanation.surface: A forecast backed up by an opinion pollster turns out to be overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Projection' reads as a forecast, which suits the pollster, but here it is the machine part CAM; 'supported by' places it above P in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes behaviour or style that is deliberately theatrical and overdone.

clue.text: Barker and Corbett essentially superior to old comic

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior to means placed above the following piece
essentially points to the essence or very centre of the name Corbett, its middle letter

parts.note: The Eagle was a British children's comic of the 1950s and 60s, home of Dan Dare

explanation.surface: Ronnie Barker and Ronnie Corbett, the Two Ronnies, are rated above some old-time comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barker and Corbett' evokes the British TV comedy double act the Two Ronnies, but Barker is the definition, a dog. The Eagle was a British boys' comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A beagle is a hound breed, and a dog is known in crosswords as a barker.

clue.text: Joint vote arranged in parliament

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the parliament's name

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of vote are set out in a different order

explanation.surface: Politicians organise a combined ballot within the legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' reads as shared, describing the vote, but it is the definition. 'arranged' gives OVET; the Dail is the lower house of Ireland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking woodwork joint shaped like a bird's tail.

clue.text: City houses exposed to typhoon's tail

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its outer covering, so the word for houses loses its first and last letters

parts.note: houses as a noun means dwellings

indicators.note: tail asks for the final letter of typhoon

explanation.surface: A city's homes lie open to the last lash of a typhoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposed' strips DWELLINGS of its outer letters to leave WELLING; 'to' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Wellington is the capital city of New Zealand.

clue.text: Diminutive type bowled no maidens, somewhat upset

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small cricketer bowled without a single maiden over and was rather disappointed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' finds DNOMAID inside the words, and 'upset' turns it round, as fits a down entry. In cricket, a maiden is an over where no runs are scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Diamond is an old printers' name for a very small size of typeface, about four and a half points.

clue.text: Comparatively weighty kitchen item picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word for the kitchen item is said and taken by its sound

parts.note: a grater is a kitchen tool for shredding cheese or vegetables

explanation.surface: A rather heavy kitchen utensil is lifted off the counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' looks like lifting the item, but it signals hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is the comparative of great, meaning more important or significant.

clue.text: Controversial European, one interrupting presenter

parts.note: a Pole is a person from Poland

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so one sits inside the presenter's letters

parts.note: MC, master of ceremonies, is a presenter or host
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A combative European keeps butting in on a TV host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupting' puts I inside MC to make MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemic as an adjective describes something argumentative and contentious.

clue.text: Spooner's had little bite in food prepared for excursion, perhaps

indicators.note: Spooner's says the first sounds of the two words are swapped, after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: lacked means had little or was short of
punch, like bite, means forcefulness or impact

explanation.surface: The Reverend Spooner's lunch had no flavour to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening letters of LACKED PUNCH, a phrase for 'had little bite', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A packed lunch is a meal made up in advance to take on a day trip or to school.

clue.text: Rogue discovered absconder returning, say, to pinch vehicle

indicators.note: discovered is read as dis-covered, its covers taken off, so the outer letters go

parts.note: an escapee is someone who has absconded, typically from prison

indicators.note: returning says the combined piece is read backwards
to pinch means to grip, so the example abbreviation wraps round the vehicle

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means here
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A villain was found out when an escaped convict came back to steal a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' is read as dis-covered, covers off; 'to pinch' wraps EG round the vehicle to give ECARG, which 'returning' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegrace is an old word for a mischievous rascal or ne'er-do-well.

clue.text: Tree branch pruned with minimum of energy

indicators.note: pruned means cut back, so the word for branch loses its last letter

parts.note: a limb is a large branch of a tree

indicators.note: minimum of means the smallest part of the word energy, its first letter

explanation.surface: A tree's branch is cut back using very little effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pruned' trims LIMB to LIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The lime, or linden, is a broadleaved tree common in European parks.

clue.text: Bakery ad broadcast first thing in the morning

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A baker's advert goes out on the radio at the crack of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' suggests radio, but it asks for the letters of BAKERY AD to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Daybreak is dawn, the very start of the morning.

clue.text: Live Geordie performer secures female financial backer

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

indicators.note: secures means holds fast, so the Geordie performer encloses the female letter

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Tyneside in North East England, abbreviated NE
an actor is a stage performer

explanation.surface: A Newcastle entertainer on stage lands a woman as sponsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live' looks like an adjective for the performer but is the verb BE. 'secures' holds the female letter. A Geordie is someone from Tyneside in North East England.
explanation.definitionFit: A benefactor is a patron who gives money to support a person or cause.

clue.text: 12 heading off to find shade

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: 12 across is DAYBREAK, and daybreak is the dawning

explanation.surface: At dawn someone sets off in search of somewhere shady.
explanation.walkthrough: The 12 refers to the answer at 12 across; its synonym DAWNING loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An awning is a canvas cover that gives shade over a shop front or window.

clue.text: Disbelief from university student being solvent around end of January

indicators.note: around says the solvent phrase is placed round the university and student letters

parts.note: being solvent is being in credit, with money in the account
L, the learner plate, stands for a student

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of January

explanation.surface: A student is amazed to find their bank account in the black at the end of January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts U and L inside IN CREDIT; Y, the end of January, follows. L for learner, from British learner-driver plates, is a crossword student.
explanation.definitionFit: Incredulity is the state of being unable or unwilling to believe something.

clue.text: Raised occasionally tender, large foreign flower that's fragrant

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, which in a down clue reads the whole piece from bottom to top
occasionally asks for every other letter of the word tender

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a flower is a river, something that flows; the Oder runs through Germany and Poland

explanation.surface: A gardener lifts a delicate, big exotic bloom that smells lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes TNE from tender; with L and ODER that is TNELODER, which 'Raised' reverses. 'Flower' means a thing that flows, a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means sweet-smelling or strongly scented, as of perfume.

clue.text: Aircraft about to be unloaded from vessel

indicators.note: unloaded from means taken off, so the word for about is removed from the ship

parts.note: a freighter is a cargo ship
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A plane is just about to be taken off a cargo ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'nearly', but it is RE, which 'to be unloaded from' removes from FREIGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter is a fast military plane built to attack other planes.

clue.text: Funny man is excited to entertain posh gathering finally

indicators.note: to entertain means to host, so the jumbled letters take in the posh letter
excited means stirred up, so the letters of man is are jumbled

parts.note: U stands for upper class, so posh

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of gathering

explanation.surface: A comic is thrilled to host a smart party at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes AMSIN from MAN IS; 'to entertain' puts U inside after AM, and G ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Amusing means entertaining or causing laughter.

clue.text: Offended whenever served meal after Mike

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the letter for Mike

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, I stay in'
to have fed someone is to have served them a meal

explanation.surface: Mike gets cross any time dinner is put in front of him.
explanation.definitionFit: Miffed is an informal word for annoyed or put out.

clue.text: Subject to review, policeman resumes keeping computer ID

indicators.note: review is read as re-view, viewing again from the other end, so the held letters run backwards
keeping means holding inside, so the answer is held within the words policeman resumes

explanation.surface: An officer picks up his inquiry, holding on to a suspect's computer login.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters EMANRESU sit inside 'policeman resumes', and 'Subject to review' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A username is the name a person uses to identify themselves when logging in to a computer system.

clue.text: Hear trial that regularly is making mistakes

indicators.note: regularly asks for letters at regular intervals, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Listening to a court case that keeps going wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every second letter of HEARTRIALTHAT spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, especially those listed in a printed book.

clue.text: Mechanic to abandon shabby style

indicators.note: to abandon means to leave, so the letters for shabby are dropped from mechanic

parts.note: mean can mean shabby or poor in appearance

explanation.surface: A mechanic is ready to give up on a scruffy look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' removes the letters M, E, A and N, scattered in that order, from MECHANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is elegance or stylishness, used as a noun here.

clue.text: Given to weeping, my Carole's potentially capturing hearts

indicators.note: capturing means taking in, so the jumbled letters take in the hearts letter
potentially means could become, so the letters of my Carole's can be made into something else

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: Carole, who steals hearts, is quick to cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges MYCAROLES and 'capturing' takes in H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymose means tearful, from the Latin word for a tear.

clue.text: Fashion, cut maybe in a striped pattern reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.words: cut maybe in a striped pattern
parts.note: a lawn mowed is cut and left in neat stripes

explanation.surface: A trendy style may involve cutting stripes into something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striped pattern' suggests fabric but describes a freshly cut lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Mode means the current fashion or style, as in 'all the mode'.

clue.text: Possible consequence of close election result, in detail

definitions.text: Possible consequence of close election result
definitions.meaning: a ..., counting the votes again, follows a very narrow result
to detail or narrate an account

explanation.surface: A tight vote leads to the ballots being counted again, in full.
explanation.definitionFit: A recount re-counts votes, and recount also means tell, relate or narrate.

clue.text: Daring act involving extremely desperate undergraduate

indicators.note: involving means including, so the stunt word wraps round the extreme letters

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last of desperate

explanation.surface: A desperate undergraduate pulls a reckless stunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like it intensifies 'desperate', but it takes only that word's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A student at university studying for a first degree is an undergraduate.
